idiom_name: hub struct with a map of subscriber channels and a Publish fan-out
implementation_notes: Go has no event bus in the standard library, so the idiom is a small hub type owning a map of subscriber channels: Subscribe returns a receive-only channel plus an unsubscribe function, Publish sends each event to every channel, and a sync.WaitGroup or context drives shutdown. Channels make the delivery policy explicit instead of implicit - unbuffered sends block the publisher, a buffered channel absorbs bursts, and a non-blocking select with default drops for slow subscribers. A classic registry of subscriber objects is justified only when consumers need rich per-topic filtering that would otherwise be re-implemented around the channel.
pitfalls: Sending on a closed channel panics: unsubscribe must delete the subscriber under the same lock Publish takes, and only the owning goroutine closes the channel.
Goroutines blocked on an unconsumed channel are not garbage collected; a subscriber that stops reading leaks its goroutine and its slot in the hub.
Shutdown must close subscriber channels or consumers ranging over them block forever.
